title: Survodutide (BI 456906): GLP-1/Glucagon Dual Agonist — Phase 3 Research Dossier
excerpt: Survodutide (BI 456906) is a once-weekly GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist with Phase 3 NEJM data showing 16.6% weight loss in obesity and Nature Medicine data showing superior liver fat reduction in MASLD. A comprehensive research overview.
content:
Research Disclaimer: Survodutide (BI 456906) is an investigational compound. It is not approved by the FDA, EMA, or any regulatory agency as of November 2026. Content is for educational and research purposes only. Not medical advice. Consult a qualified healthcare provider before making any health decisions.

What Is Survodutide?

Survodutide (development code: BI 456906) is a once-weekly injectable unimolecular dual agonist developed jointly by Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma. It simultaneously activates two metabolically important G-protein coupled receptors: the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucagon receptor (GCGR).

While most widely discussed obesity drugs — semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide — are built around GLP-1 receptor agonism, survodutide's co-activation of the glucagon receptor introduces a second, complementary mechanism: direct hepatic fat mobilization and increased energy expenditure. This makes survodutide particularly relevant not only for weight loss but also for metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly known as NAFLD/NASH.

As of November 2026, survodutide has completed multiple Phase 3 trials across obesity and MASLD populations, with data published in the New England Journal of Medicine and Nature Medicine.

Mechanism of Action

Survodutide's dual receptor engagement produces distinct, additive metabolic effects:

GLP-1 Receptor (GLP-1R) Effects

  • Appetite suppression via hypothalamic and brainstem satiety circuits
  • Slowed gastric emptying (reduced food intake rate)
  • Glucose-dependent insulin secretion enhancement
  • Reduced hepatic glucose production

Glucagon Receptor (GCGR) Effects

  • Stimulates hepatic fatty acid oxidation (beta-oxidation) — directly reduces liver fat
  • Increases thermogenesis and energy expenditure beyond GLP-1 effects alone
  • Reduces hepatic de novo lipogenesis
  • Activates brown adipose tissue

Preclinical pharmacology of survodutide, published in Nature Communications (PMC9679702), demonstrated that the dual agonist produced substantially greater weight loss and fat mass reduction compared to selective GLP-1 or glucagon agonists alone in rodent obesity models. A 2026 mechanistic review in Obesity Reviews (PubMed 42822760) summarized the clinical rationale and remaining uncertainties including the theoretical concern about glucagon-driven hyperglycemia in diabetic populations.

Key Research Findings

Phase 2 (Dose-Finding)

DoseWeight Loss (46 weeks)Placebo
Survodutide 4.8 mg–18.7%–2.3%

Phase 3: SYNCHRONIZE-1 (Obesity Without T2DM) — NEJM, ADA 2026

Population: 1,033 adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least one weight-related complication, without type 2 diabetes.

  • Weight loss at 76 weeks: Up to –16.6% (efficacy estimand) vs. –3.2% placebo
  • Results published simultaneously in the New England Journal of Medicine at ADA 2026
  • Significant improvements in cardiometabolic risk markers including waist circumference, blood pressure, and lipids

Phase 3: SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD (Obesity with Liver Disease) — Nature Medicine, June 2026

Population: 368 adults with obesity and confirmed MASLD (excess liver fat on imaging).

  • Body weight reduction: –12.2% vs. –1.0% placebo at 48 weeks
  • Liver fat reduction: >30% reduction in liver fat achieved by the majority of participants
  • Visceral and liver fat: 34% visceral fat reduction; 63% liver fat reduction in a pre-specified analysis subset
  • Notable lean mass preservation relative to total weight lost
  • Published: Nature Medicine, June 7, 2026

Phase 3: SYNCHRONIZE-2 (Obesity with T2DM) — October 2026

Population: Adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

  • Weight loss at 76 weeks: Up to –13.1% vs. –3.1% placebo
  • Topline results announced October 1, 2026; full publication pending

SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT (Cardiovascular Outcomes)

Trial completed October 2026; results and publication pending as of this writing.

Dosing in Research

Note: The following reflects protocols used in clinical trials only. Survodutide is not approved or available commercially.

  • Route: Subcutaneous injection (once weekly)
  • Doses studied: Dose escalation from low starting doses up to 4.8–6.0 mg once weekly in Phase 3
  • Duration: 48–76 weeks in Phase 3 trials
  • Titration: Gradual dose escalation used to minimize gastrointestinal adverse effects

Frequently Asked Questions

How does survodutide differ from semaglutide and tirzepatide for weight loss?

Survodutide activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors simultaneously, a combination that adds energy expenditure and direct hepatic fat oxidation to the appetite suppression of GLP-1 agonism. Semaglutide is a pure GLP-1 agonist. Tirzepatide adds GIP receptor activation to GLP-1. The glucagon receptor component in survodutide is particularly effective at reducing liver fat — Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD showed >30% liver fat reduction in most participants at 48 weeks, published in Nature Medicine (2026). Survodutide's SYNCHRONIZE-1 showed 16.6% weight loss at 76 weeks (NEJM, ADA 2026), comparable to tirzepatide and semaglutide but with a potentially superior liver-specific metabolic profile.

What is MASLD and why is survodutide particularly relevant for it?

MASLD stands for Metabolic-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (formerly NAFLD/NASH), a spectrum of liver conditions driven by excess liver fat accumulation linked to metabolic syndrome, obesity, and insulin resistance. Survodutide's glucagon receptor component directly stimulates hepatic fatty acid oxidation and reduces de novo lipogenesis, mechanisms that GLP-1 agonists alone do not significantly engage. In SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD (Phase 3, N=368), survodutide achieved 12.2% body weight reduction and >30% liver fat reduction in most participants at 48 weeks vs. 1.0% weight reduction in the placebo arm, published in Nature Medicine in June 2026.

Is survodutide safe for people with type 2 diabetes?

Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-2 specifically enrolled adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, reporting 13.1% weight loss vs. 3.1% placebo at 76 weeks (announced October 1, 2026). Safety in this population was consistent with the GLP-1 drug class: nausea, vomiting, and gastrointestinal side effects were most common. The glucagon receptor component theoretically raises a concern about glucagon-driven glucose elevation in diabetes, but this was studied and managed in the trial protocol. Full safety data from peer-reviewed publication of SYNCHRONIZE-2 should be reviewed. Survodutide is not approved by the FDA or EMA as of November 2026.

Research Limitations and Open Questions

  • No FDA or EMA approval as of November 2026; regulatory filing timeline not announced
  • SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT cardiovascular safety data pending publication
  • SYNCHRONIZE-2 full peer-reviewed publication pending (only topline announced)
  • Long-term durability beyond 76 weeks not yet established in Phase 3
  • Comparative efficacy vs. tirzepatide and retatrutide not available from head-to-head trials
  • Glucagon-driven hyperglycemia risk requires monitoring in diabetic populations
